songs.title: the one
songs.verdict: Roller-rink funk with horns, a raspy falsetto and zero brooding: a love song built to make a room move.
songs.body:
Gabriel Jacoby is a self-taught Tampa-raised multi-instrumentalist, and “the one” is his case that a love song doesn't need to sulk. He has said he wanted something happy people could feel free to groove to, and the press read it the same way: buzzed-out, funkified pop with a nod to the South's roller-disco era, complete with a video shot at a hometown skating rink.

**Melody & hook:** built for the floor, with a pounding bassline and rhythmic guitars doing the pushing. **Vocals & delivery:** a raspy falsetto backed by riffing, harmonizing singers; one critic heard Al Green-like peaks. **Production:** sharp horns and gritty electric guitar give it bite instead of gloss. **Lyrics:** plain admiration for a lover, no angst.

It anchored the gutta child EP, which drew a strong 8 from The Needle Drop, and The Current made it a Song of the Day. The knock: the retro-funk blueprint is familiar, and the words stay simple.
songs.scout_note: From Marku's Apple Music library (18 plays). Big One: ~2.9M monthly, PULSE Records/Concord. Press: Stereogum (Sep 19 2025), EARMILK (horns, raspy falsetto, roller-disco), Atwood (EP out Nov 14 2025), Needle Drop 8/10 on gutta child EP, The Current Song of the Day (Feb 2026). YouTube from EARMILK embed. Doubt: Atwood links IG 'gabrieljacoby' vs given 'gabrieljcoby' - check.

songs.title: keep steady
songs.verdict: The viral one that put Apex, NC on the map: moody, R&B-tinted trap that sets its mood in seconds.
songs.body:
sosocamo, born Cameron Sanders in Apex, North Carolina, is the rapper who turned camo-and-ghillie Bass Pro styling into a brand, and “keep steady” is the song that made it work. It went viral, crossed roughly 70 million Spotify plays by early 2026, and earned him his first distribution deal.

**Melody & hook:** The FADER hears trap's bounce filtered through R&B mood-setting; PRNCPLS says it sets a mood almost immediately. **Vocals & delivery:** smooth, sung-rap tones he credits to years in a church choir. **Production:** part of the Grayto-steered sound with pulled-back drums and room left around the hook. It's also the shortest track on no service.

Replay is the whole story: short, low-key, built for loops. The knock is that the lane (Future meets Brent Faiyaz after midnight) is crowded, and the press talks about mood more than words.
songs.scout_note: From Marku's Apple Music library (13 plays). Big One: ~2.8M monthly, Apex NC; Wikipedia lists label Broke. Press: The FADER (Feb 26 2026, ~70M Spotify plays, R&B-leaning trap, Future/Brent Faiyaz/Pi'erre Bourne), PRNCPLS (Big Country sound, shortest track on no service). Later also on big country (2026). Exec producer Grayto; track-level producer credits not found. No IG on official source.

songs.title: Wake Up
songs.verdict: Laid-back bedroom disco about sleepwalking through your own life: a funky bassline and a shrug of a vocal.
songs.body:
Kowloon is an LA musician and filmmaker who wrote, played, recorded and mixed his debut album Come Over alone in a home studio. “Wake Up” arrived ahead of it and became one of its defining tracks; Satin Jackets later called it a hit and remixed it in 2026. Kowloon describes it as a song about sleepwalking through a life that no longer feels like your own.

**Melody & hook:** reviewers call it chilled, catchy and easy-drifting, a lo-fi rock/indie-electro blend. **Production:** a funky bassline leads, with dreamy guitars and a gliding groove over his vintage drum-machine palette. **Vocals & delivery:** understated and a little detached, which suits the theme. **Lyrics:** the malaise is in the concept more than any big line.

It's a song that ages well on repeat because it never pushes. The knock: the detachment can read as flat, and Come Over plays in the same mellow register throughout.
songs.scout_note: From Marku's Apple Music library (9 plays). Big One: ~1.1M monthly, LA one-man project. Sources: Mix It All Up review (Apr 19 2020, artist quote on theme, funky bassline), Satin Jackets remix post (calls it a hit, editorial playlists), We All Want Someone/WtMM/Maison Kitsune on Come Over. Doubt: Satin Jackets dates Come Over to 2021; another Spotify ID (3FKJaFrmNNDuYeUSY8HhmF) exists for the 2020 single.

songs.title: Gimme A Sign
songs.verdict: Detroit stream-of-consciousness rap over broken vocal chops and booming 808s, searching for direction out loud.
songs.body:
Luhh Dyl is a young Detroit rapper who broke through with “LaLaLa” and his shopping-cart “Cart Music” clips, and is now on 300. “Gimme A Sign” followed his Hear My Cry album with a video, and finds him taking stock of his life and career as he looks toward 2026.

**Production:** the release notes describe broken vocal samples and booming Michigan 808s. **Vocals & delivery:** a stream-of-consciousness flow; writers often note his slightly behind-the-beat pocket. **Lyrics:** introspective, a search for purpose rather than a flex. **Melody & hook:** carried more by the chopped samples than a sung chorus.

Coverage is mostly label-driven, so the case rests on the replay count and his lane. The knock: introspective Detroit rap over chopped samples is a busy field, and nothing in the write-ups says what sets this one apart.
songs.scout_note: From Marku's Apple Music library (12 plays). Big One: ~814K monthly, Detroit, 300 Entertainment. Sources: Audible Treats press release (Nov 20 2025: broken vocal samples, Michigan 808s, life-purpose theme), Audible Treats bio (IG @luhhdyl). Spotify/Tidal/Amazon/Deezer from official luhhdyl.lnk.to page; YouTube = official video; SoundCloud from search (uploader account name unconfirmed). Producer not named. Press is PR-driven.

songs.title: high 5ive'
songs.verdict: A short, self-steered single from an East Atlanta artist-producer who blends rap with church-raised R&B.
songs.body:
Destin Laurel is an East Atlanta artist-producer and former church drummer who taught himself to write, produce, mix and master, and runs his own imprint, klarity. Press has placed him between rap, R&B and neo-soul, with comparisons to 6lack, Bryson Tiller and PARTYNEXTDOOR. “high 5ive'” is a sub-three-minute single (2:57) from October 2024, co-produced by PLANTCHAM.

**Production:** his work is described as intricate, often reworking samples into new emotional contexts. **Vocals & delivery:** rap rooted, with gospel and R&B in the blend. **Lyrics:** writers credit him with mature writing, though no source details this song.

No write-up covers this single itself, so this draft leans on his lane and the replay count. The knock is unknowable until a listen: whether it stands out from a crowded melodic rap/R&B field.
songs.scout_note: From Marku's Apple Music library (11 plays). Big One: ~532K monthly, East Atlanta, klarity. imprint. Track-level press not found; Deezer confirms Oct 16 2024, 2:57, (P) klarity. Artist context: Lyrical Lemonade (Searching For Klarity EP), note.com profile (self-producer, church drummer, klarity label). PLANTCHAM credit from input only, not independently confirmed. No IG on official source (SoundCloud: destinlaurel).

songs.title: Dirty Shoes
songs.verdict: A producer-turned-pop-artist single from his 2026 album run: emotion first, built by a beatmaker's hands.
songs.body:
Presley Regier started placing beats at 13, signed to Bird Vision and produced for Tyga, Coco Jones and Doja Cat before stepping out as an artist, opening Tate McRae's tour along the way. “Dirty Shoes” (3:29) came out in July 2026 and sits as track six on his album Sensitive to the room, sensitive to the sound.

**Production:** his solo pop is built around emotion, with bright synths, cinematic strings and sweeping melodies; the 2026 era added analog synths with producer Luka Kloser. **Melody & hook:** writers have compared his style to New Order, Foster The People and MGMT. **Vocals & delivery:** nearby singles are described with a casual, hazy delivery. No source describes this song's lyrics.

With 14 plays it's one of the library's more replayed picks. The knock: coverage names the single but never describes it, so its specific strengths need a listen.
songs.scout_note: From Marku's Apple Music library (14 plays). Big One: ~464K monthly, Bird Vision (BMI spotlight confirms Bird Vision; Roddy Ricch link from input). Sources: BMI Indie Spotlight (Dirty Shoes due Jul 10), Coda Music (3:29, track 6 on album), Melodicmag (Bug, New Order/FTP/MGMT comps), ArtistRack (Shuteye). No song-level description found anywhere. Single page: open.spotify.com/album/6SwrktkcPV7bV8Ir9hEbOQ. No IG on official source.

songs.title: I Might
songs.verdict: Hazy cloud rap with a soul streak from a 20-year-old Brit who already has Matty Healy's attention.
songs.body:
Saam Sultan is a 20-year-old British rapper raised between London, Brighton and Florida, now on Darkroom, and one of the more talked-about young UK names: V Man, Numéro and Clunk have all profiled him, and Matty Healy noticed him early. “I Might” is a July 2025 standalone single from the run before his Seraphim EP.

**Production:** his sound is described as hazy cloud-rap texture moving between ethereal passages and trap-leaning beats with heavy sliding subs. **Vocals & delivery:** a soul, R&B and pop blend that reviewers set alongside Frank Ocean. **Lyrics:** writers point to introspective, fashion-forward writing; nothing documents this song's words.

Thirteen plays and a loved mark make it a library favorite. The knock: the press covers the artist, not this single, and the cloud-rap haze can blur from track to track.
songs.scout_note: From Marku's Apple Music library (13 plays). Big One: Loved. ~431K monthly, Darkroom (Interscope) per input (no source checked names the label). Sources: V Man (cloud-rap textures), Clunk (May 2026, Frank Ocean comp, glissando subs, Matty Healy), Numero NL (Seraphim EP). None mention I Might. YouTube/Tidal from search results titled 'Saam Sultan - I Might'. No IG on official source.

songs.title: Sunny London
songs.verdict: Deep, jazzy house from a Lisbon producer: a four-minute warm-weather groove on PoolHaus.
songs.body:
sometimes jah is a producer and DJ who moved from Lisbon to Sydney and Madrid and back again, and works mostly in deep, jazzy house; the Bandcamp also carries edits like an after-hours Sade rework. “Sunny London” (3:56) is the lead side of a two-track PoolHaus single from November 2023, paired with “Café Le Matin”.

**Groove:** in his lane that means a steady, unhurried house pulse aimed at warm sets rather than peak-time. **Sound design:** jazzy colour is the documented calling card. **Hook** and **Build & drop:** no source describes this track's structure, so judge those on a listen.

It earned eleven plays, which says it works as background and as a repeat. The knock: deep jazzy house is a crowded shelf, and with no write-ups it's hard to say what lifts this above the playlist pack.
songs.scout_note: From Marku's Apple Music library (11 plays). Big One: ~341K monthly, Lisbon. Deezer: Nov 13 2023, (P) PoolHaus Ltd, 3:56, B-side Cafe Le Matin. Bandcamp bio: deep, jazzy house; Sade after-hours edit. No press on the track found; instrumental assumed from lane, confirm on listen.

songs.title: URSNMINE (feat. Norah's World)
songs.verdict: NYC alt-rap meets Norah's World's R&B on a duet the pair say reached BBC Radio.
songs.body:
3ee is an NYC alt hip-hop/R&B artist whose catalogue runs about 54 million Spotify streams, led by “OVR”. “URSNMINE” pairs him with Norah's World, a West Palm Beach-bred singer who calls him her closest collaborator. It came out in July 2023 on SUPERNOVA WORLDWIDE.

**Vocals & delivery:** a two-voice track; Norah describes her style as alternative R&B with layered, 1990s-leaning harmonies. **Lyrics:** the publisher lists two writers, Austin Keller Broadway and Norah Seide; no source unpacks the words. **Production** and **Melody & hook:** undocumented.

Norah says the song did well, with plays on BBC Radio and an Atlanta station. That's the extent of the record, so this draft stays middle-of-the-road until a listen decides it.
songs.scout_note: From Marku's Apple Music library (10 plays). CONFLICT CHECK: an interview says Norah's World's Florida producer was 'markü leone' (likely Marku); disclose if he worked on this. Half Moon BK interview: markü leone produced a Norah EP in Florida; URSNMINE not credited to him there. TRO Essex lists writers Broadway/Seide only. kworb: 3ee ~54M total streams. No Spotify link verified.

songs.title: Everybody Knows (feat. Mattvv)
songs.verdict: A freestyle that turned into a single: candid, laid-back South Florida rap that's honest about the past but still small in scale.
songs.body:
“Everybody Knows” pairs Marku Leone with Broward County rapper Mattvv, a regular collaborator. It's the one song here with a write-up: a 2022 Brazilian blog roundup said it started as a freestyle and called it hip-hop and rap vocals over a relaxed beat.

**Lyrics:** per that write-up, he raps about what he'd been dealing with lately, and about moving past old wounds, which gives it a relatable center. **Vocals & delivery:** rapped, with Mattvv on the feature. **Production** is described only as laid-back; at 2:46 it doesn't overstay.

The freestyle origin is both the appeal and the limit: it reads as candid and loose rather than a built-out hook record. One small blog mention (via a submission platform) and no playlisting on record put it in the middle of the scale until someone actually listens.
songs.scout_note: OWNER'S OWN SONG (Marku Leone) — add a disclosure if published. S. FL producer, ~1.1K Spotify monthly; own Verde/Casaverde imprint; own plays ignored. Spotify single released Apr 20 2022, 2:46, credited Marku Leone, Mattvv. Only press: Os Garotos de Liverpool Musosoup Singles #20 (May 2022, curator-submission roundup) – hip-hop vocals, relaxed instrumental, began as freestyle. Mattvv (Broward, 72 monthly listeners) also lists it on Slaps. No Apple link verified.

songs.title: Gulf Coast
songs.verdict: An early cut from his 2019 debut EP that left almost no public trace; the place-name title promises more than the record shows.
songs.body:
“Gulf Coast” comes from Red Rüm, among Marku Leone's first releases in November 2019, when his Apple Music artist page first appeared. He's a South Florida producer-artist, and the title points at home turf.

**What's documented:** almost nothing. No reviews, credits or descriptions of this song turned up, and the EP isn't listed on his current streaming pages. **Production** would be his own, since he works mainly as a producer, but that's inference, not a source.

It's early catalog with no reception to weigh, so it sits at mid-scale by default. A critic has to judge this one on the listen alone.
songs.scout_note: OWNER'S OWN SONG (Marku Leone) — add a disclosure if published. S. FL producer, ~1.1K Spotify monthly; own Verde/Casaverde imprint; own plays ignored. No source found for Red Rüm EP or 'Gulf Coast' (not on current Apple artist page or in search). Genre 'pop' is only the Apple artist-level tag. No links verified. Release date from input. songs.title: Cherry
songs.verdict: A debut-era single with no public footprint, so a fair read waits on the listen.
songs.body:
“Cherry” is one of Marku Leone's first singles, from November 2019, the same month as the Red Rüm EP. He was just starting out then as a South Florida producer who also records his own vocals.

**What's documented:** nothing beyond the release itself. No press, playlist placement or credits came up, and it doesn't appear on his current Apple Music page. Melody, vocals and production can't be described without inventing them.

As early work with no reception on record, it gets a neutral starting score. Expect it to sound like a first step next to the 2023–2026 singles, but that's for the critic's ears to confirm.

songs.title: Beautiful Mess
songs.verdict: A Florida–Philly link-up with a little more reach than most of his catalog; it holds together and doesn't overreach.
songs.body:
“Beautiful Mess” comes from Nü Heroine, a four-track EP Marku Leone shared with Philadelphia artist Pops Tuna in August 2021, with Jaces Phantasm featured elsewhere on the project. Pops Tuna tags his own work alternative, garage rock and lo-fi, and the two had already teamed up on his “Girls Cry” that June.

**Reach:** it has an official YouTube upload and a TikTok sound page, and both artists showed up on BIRP!'s September 2021 indie playlist, though it's unconfirmed which track made the list. **Production & vocals:** no source describes them; it runs 2:46.

Of his older songs, this one got the most outside traction, mostly because of Pops Tuna's bigger audience (about 11K monthly listeners against Marku's 1.1K). There's still no press verdict, so it lands just on the better side of middling.
songs.scout_note: OWNER'S OWN SONG (Marku Leone) — add a disclosure if published. S. FL producer, ~1.1K Spotify monthly; own Verde/Casaverde imprint; own plays ignored. Indie Playlist Sept 2021 lists both as featured artists (track unconfirmed). Pops Tuna: Philly, 11.3K monthly, Bandcamp tags alt/garage/lofi. Genre is borrowed from Pops Tuna's tags.

songs.title: Circles
songs.verdict: A short indie-pop turn with Mattvv that shows up among his most-played songs on Apple Music, which is the best sign it has.
songs.body:
“Circles” reunites Marku Leone with Mattvv, his most frequent partner, on an August 2023 single from his Verde imprint. Apple files it as indie pop, a step away from the hip-hop framing of “Everybody Knows.”

**Shape:** 2:39, a single with no remixes or extras. **Reach:** it's #2 in Apple Music's Top Songs on his artist page, behind only “Granite,” a sign listeners keep finding it. **Vocals, melody & production:** no outside source describes them, so the critic's ear has to fill this in.

Its place in his top songs is the best thing going for it, but that ranking is within a small catalog of around a thousand monthly listeners, with no reviews. A modest lean toward the good side, no more.

Spotify link not found. No press.

songs.title: Feels Like Sümmer
songs.verdict: A summer-titled duet his own team still puts out front, but there's no outside response yet to back it up.
songs.body:
“Feels Like Sümmer” is a June 2024 duet with an artist named Divina. It still appears among the featured covers on Casaverde, the management and creative group that hosts Marku Leone's links, so his own team clearly counts it among the highlights.

**What's documented:** the pairing, the date, and the seasonal title. No press, credits, length or descriptions surfaced, and it's not among his current Apple Music top songs. **Vocals:** a two-artist credit, but who sings what isn't on record.

No reception means a neutral score. Note that it's a different song from the many other “Feels Like Summer” tracks, so a critic should check the umlaut spelling before pulling links.

Genre 'pop' = artist-level tag, not documented for this song. No links verified. NO VERIFIED LINK FOUND: add your own link before publishing.

songs.title: bad habits die hard (feat. trapzart)
songs.verdict: The title track of a three-song, six-minute drop: quick sketches, not a statement, and too little on record to rate it higher.
songs.body:
“bad habits die hard” is the title track of a short 2025 release on Verde. The package runs three songs in about six minutes, with Mattvv on the other two (“thought you were in love” and “was it real?”), and trapzart, who also appears on his “IDKHOW” and “SOBER MIND,” on this one.

**Format:** these are very short songs; the one closing track with a listed time runs 1:40, so expect sketch-length cuts. **Genre:** Apple files the release as alternative. **Vocals, hook & production:** no source describes them.

The two Mattvv tracks show up in his Apple top songs list and the title track doesn't, which says little either way. With no press, it stays mid-scale.
songs.scout_note: OWNER'S OWN SONG (Marku Leone) — add a disclosure if published. S. FL producer, ~1.1K Spotify monthly; own Verde/Casaverde imprint; own plays ignored. Apple lists release date Feb 14 2025 (input said Jan 2025; used Apple's date). 3 songs ~6 min, Alternative, ℗ 2025 Verde. Title-track trapzart feature NOT confirmed on a fetched page (input says so; trapzart is a confirmed collaborator elsewhere). Apple link is the release, not the track. No press.

songs.title: In the Fog (feat. SLPYJAYY)
songs.verdict: The opening of his SLPYJAYY partnership, tidy at 2:36 and in his top five on Apple, with nothing outside his own pages yet.
songs.body:
“In the Fog” is a September 2025 single featuring SLPYJAYY, the first of two collaborations between them. It came out under Casaverde, the management and creative outfit behind his recent releases.

**Shape:** 2:36, one track, filed by Apple as alternative. **Reach:** it ranks fifth in his Apple Music top songs, so within his own catalog it found some listeners. **Vocals & production:** no source describes the song's sound, the split of verses, or who produced it.

The partnership was strong enough to bring back for “Fukkit” in January. On paper, though, this is a small-audience single with no press, so it sits in the middle until someone listens.
songs.scout_note: OWNER'S OWN SONG (Marku Leone) — add a disclosure if published. S. FL producer, ~1.1K Spotify monthly; own Verde/Casaverde imprint; own plays ignored. Apple: Sep 26 2025, 2:36, Alternative, ℗ 2025 Casaverde. #5 in Apple Top Songs on artist page. Song URL https://music.apple.com/us/album/in-the-fog-feat-slpyjayy/1839839279?i=1839839286. No info found on SLPYJAYY. No press, no Spotify link found.

songs.title: Fukkit
songs.verdict: A New Year's Day reunion with SLPYJAYY that runs longer than his usual singles and ranks near the top of his catalog, but no press has weighed in.
songs.body:
“Fukkit” brought Marku Leone and SLPYJAYY back together, this time as co-leads, on New Year's Day 2026, three months after “In the Fog.” It's out on Casaverde.

**Shape:** at 3:25 it's one of his longer singles, since much of his recent work runs under three minutes. **Genre:** Apple files it as alternative. **Reach:** fourth in his Apple Music top songs. **Lyrics & vocals:** the title sets a don't-care mood, but nothing on record describes what's said or how it's delivered.

It's a fair sign that the pairing came back and the song holds a top-five spot in his catalog, but that's a small pond. With no reviews or playlists to cite, it stays mid-scale.
songs.scout_note: OWNER'S OWN SONG (Marku Leone) — add a disclosure if published. S. FL producer, ~1.1K Spotify monthly; own Verde/Casaverde imprint; own plays ignored. Apple: Jan 1 2026, 3:25, Alternative, ℗ 2026 Casaverde, credited Marku Leone & SLPYJAYY. #4 in Apple Top Songs on artist page. No press, no Spotify link found.

songs.title: Paradise
songs.verdict: His newest single, a co-written rap track with Xander Woods. It's already #3 in his catalog, but there's no outside verdict.
songs.body:
“Paradise” is Marku Leone's most recent release, a March 2026 single with Xander Woods. Deezer credits the pair as co-writers, and Casaverde puts the cover first in its featured releases.

**Genre & shape:** Apple files it as hip-hop/rap, his first single in that lane in a while after a run of alternative releases, and it runs 2:38. **Reach:** it's already third in his Apple Music top songs. **Vocals & production:** no source describes the beat, the hook or how the two split the song.

Promising signs for a newer track, but it's all from his own channels and streaming rankings, with no press or playlist adds. Middle of the scale until a critic hears it.
songs.scout_note: OWNER'S OWN SONG (Marku Leone) — add a disclosure if published. S. FL producer, ~1.1K Spotify monthly; own Verde/Casaverde imprint; own plays ignored. Apple: Mar 13 2026, 2:38, Hip-Hop/Rap, ℗ 2026 Casaverde. #3 in Apple Top Songs. Deezer album 933130721 credits composers Marku Leone & Xander Woods (via Xander Woods Deezer page). Featured first on casa.donebyverde.com. No press, no Spotify link found.

songs.title: i get so high
songs.verdict: Two Casaverde-adjacent rappers trade a short, hazy 2:41 on getting lifted; tidy, but nothing on paper sets it apart from the pack.
songs.body:
“i get so high” pairs trapzart, a prolific Hip-Hop/Rap catalog artist with a steady run of 2026 singles, with SLPYJAYY, whose alt-rap work comes out through Casaverde. It's a one-track single, 2:41 long, filed by Apple as underground rap.

**Vocals & delivery:** a two-voice record, so the trade-off between them is the point; check whether they push each other or just split the time. **Melody & hook:** the title is the hook, and at this length it has to land fast. **Production:** no producer credit is listed; judge the beat on the listen.

No press or playlist trail yet, so this is a starting draft. Replay rides on the hook. The knock: it's one more short collab in a busy feed, and it needs a distinct idea to stand out.
songs.scout_note: OWNER'S CIRCLE (collaborator of Marku Leone) — disclose if published. Marku: 4 plays. Apple: single, 1 track 2:41, genre Underground Rap, ℗ 2026 Casaverde. Song page says Aug 9, album page says Aug 31, 2026. SLPYJAYY Apple artist: music.apple.com/us/artist/slpyjayy/1709729037. trapzart was featured on Marku's FUCKWHATYOUHURD. No Spotify link found, no press, no producer credits, no listener counts. Evidence: thin.

songs.title: graveyard
songs.verdict: A fresh, compact SLPYJAYY single that ships with its own sped-up twin; promising, but still has to prove itself outside the circle.
songs.body:
SLPYJAYY has been building steadily: a 2025 album, Dreamstate, a string of 2026 singles and features with Marku Leone and Michaiah. “graveyard” landed Oct 30, 2026 on Casaverde, filed as alternative rap, and comes as a two-track single with a “(fast)” version, about four minutes in all.

**Melody & hook:** the sped-up cut suggests a song built for clips and replays, so the hook has to carry at both speeds. **Vocals & delivery:** judge on the listen whether the voice holds its mood. **Production:** no credits are listed.

There's no write-up or playlist trail yet; Marku's six plays in under two weeks are a small sign it sticks. The limit: at two minutes, with the sped-up version doing extra work, it reads more like a sketch than a statement.
songs.scout_note: OWNER'S CIRCLE (collaborator of Marku Leone) — disclose if published. Marku: 6 plays (released Oct 30, 2026, so recent). Apple: 2-track single (graveyard + graveyard (fast), ~2:00 each), genre Alternative Rap, ℗ 2026 Casaverde. SLPYJAYY appears on Marku's 'In the Fog'. No Spotify link found, no press, no credits, no listener count. Evidence: thin.

songs.title: Cathedral
songs.verdict: Fourteen short lo-fi garage songs in thirty minutes, held together by a three-part title suite; a scrappy, prolific record that rewards fans more than newcomers.
songs.body:
Pops Tuna is a prolific Philadelphia-tagged DIY act whose Bandcamp runs deep: Antipop Inc., Sweetness, Bitterness and, after this, Slacker. Cathedral is a 14-track, 30-minute album tagged alternative, garage rock and lofi, with features from Jaces Phantasm and 360 Quickscopes.

**Structure:** most songs land around two minutes, and the title returns three times (Cathedral, II and III), the last two the longest cuts, which suggests an arc rather than a loose dump. **Production:** the lo-fi tag sets expectations; rough edges are part of the plan. **Lyrics:** song titles like Demons, Curse and End My Life point to dark material, but judge the words on the listen.

The knock: with this many releases this fast, quality control is the open question, and Bandcamp shows only two supporters so far.
songs.scout_note: OWNER'S CIRCLE (collaborator of Marku Leone) — disclose if published. No play count given. Bandcamp: released Oct 29, 2025, 14 tracks ~30:05, tags alternative/garage rock/lofi/Philadelphia, 2 supporters. Apple genre Rock. IG popstuna from Bandcamp profile links. Pops Tuna is on Marku's 'Beautiful Mess' and 'Nü Heroine'. No reviews of Cathedral found (albumblitz has a page for Slacker only, tags folk/rock). Spotify album for Cathedral not found. Evidence: thin.

songs.title: Take The Light
songs.verdict: The title track of a five-song joint EP between Larry Paz and Marku Leone; there's no outside reception yet, so the listen has to decide this one.
songs.body:
Larry Paz is a hip-hop artist with singles going back to 2018 and a 2020 album, Something Good. Take The Light is a joint EP with Marku Leone, released Jan 31, 2025 through Familia Criativa: five songs, about 13 minutes, filed as alternative rap. This is the title track.

**Vocals & delivery:** a two-artist record, so the chemistry between the voices is what to judge. **Melody & hook:** a title track should be the EP's clearest idea. **Production:** no credits are public.

There's no outside reception to lean on, and Larry Paz's Spotify page shows a few hundred monthly listeners, so this sits mid-scale until someone listens. The limit: a short EP with a small footprint needs a hook that travels.

Apple link is the EP, not the song. Larry Paz Spotify: 367 monthly listeners (open.spotify.com/artist/0NlDYgOnxkA4KT0Osj4Zro). No press. Owner on it, so the score must come from an independent listen. Evidence: thin.

songs.title: With My Girls
songs.verdict: A 2:40 girls'-night R&B single from an indie singer still early in her catalog; easy to like, but nothing documented yet lifts it above pleasant.
songs.body:
Divina is an independent R&B singer with a small, focused catalog: the 2023 Fantasy EP, then two 2024 singles, Feels Like Sümmer and this one. “With My Girls” came out July 1, 2024 on her own Divine Aura Sounds, and runs 2:40.

**Vocals & delivery:** R&B lives or dies on the voice, and that's what to check first. **Melody & hook:** the title promises a friends-first anthem, so the chorus should feel communal. **Production:** no credits are listed.

There's no press or playlist trail; Marku's four plays are a modest nod. The limit: it's a short single from an artist who hasn't released since 2024, apart from a 2026 feature, so there's little momentum around it.
songs.scout_note: OWNER'S CIRCLE (collaborator of Marku Leone) — disclose if published. Marku: 4 plays. Apple: single, Jul 1, 2024, 2:40, R&B/Soul, ℗ 2024 DIVINE AURA SOUNDS. Spotify track verified (WITH MY GIRLS, Jul 1, 2024, 2:40). Search results also showed Deezer/TIDAL 'Divina' artist pages, but there are other artists with that name, so I left them out. No bio, press or listener count. Evidence: thin.

songs.title: worldgirl
songs.verdict: A tight six-song, fifteen-minute EP from a West Palm Beach-raised alt-R&B singer with real press behind her, and big-name production credits on at least one cut.
songs.body:
Norah's World is a West Palm Beach-raised, New York-based singer who calls her music alternative R&B, and press has picked up on her: GROWN and Half Moon BK have both profiled her, praising whispered vocals over drill, belted runs and playful, tongue-in-cheek writing. She's also in the trio bbyblu with 3ee and Kenji, whose “561” reached a million streams. worldgirl, out Aug 28, 2026, is six songs in about 15 minutes.

**Vocals & delivery:** her '90s-R&B-trained layered harmonies are the selling point. **Production:** Shazam credits list Ojivolta as producer on “2NITE,” with waytoofresco co-producing. **Melody & hook:** short tracks (closer “shake it up” runs 1:36) keep it moving.

The limit: at 15 minutes it plays more like a snapshot than a full statement.

Press: grownmag.com (Dec 2025, IG @n0rahsw0rld), halfmoonbk.com (2023, names markü leone as an early collaborator). No Spotify album URL found. Evidence: ok.

songs.title: CONSCIENCE
songs.verdict: A sub-two-minute solo single from a rapper who releases constantly; it's quick and self-released, and nothing documented singles it out from the stream.
songs.body:
trapzart puts out music at a remarkable rate: seven albums since 2023, a run of 2026 singles, and a long list of features. “CONSCIENCE” came out Feb 22, 2026, self-released and filed as Hip-Hop/Rap, and runs 1:52.

**Lyrics:** an all-caps one-word title like this hints at something more inward than his party records, but judge that on the listen. **Melody & hook:** under two minutes leaves room for one idea, so it has to hit at once. **Production:** no credits listed.

There's no press or playlist trail, and three plays from Marku is a light signal. The knock: in a catalog this crowded, a short single needs a standout hook to matter.

Apple lists a second 'Trapzart' artist (CA, id 1684606254), so check it's the right one. No Spotify link verified, no press. Evidence: thin.
